title: The Brief note on the table
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：brief　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 brief 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the fisherman wrote of ① a brief note on the table in the logbook, and everybody in the harbour said at once that it was ② briefer than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the fisherman, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the brief ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the briefest note on the table anybody in the harbour had ever seen, or so the logbook for July 1942 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too brief to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the boatman who had come to help; the brief ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a brief visit in spring, and said that no boatman in his right mind would call it ⑥ as brief as the visit in spring they had once had in the old harbour. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was brief or not, and he said so.

By 1955 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the logbook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something brief, and nothing besides. The boatman from the next harbour called the whole plan ⑧ quite brief; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the logbook kept the names of the brief ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1958, for the whole place, she wrote of another brief note on the table in the same logbook, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ briefer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The briefest visit in spring in the whole harbour, she said in 1960, was the one she could never quite name; the brief ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 简短（前置定语 a brief note on the table：1948 年渔人在航海日志里记下的那件简短的字条）
B. adj. 简短／短暂（比较级 briefer than：文中两处，一处比桌上的字条，一处比预想）
C. adj. 简短／短暂（最高级 the briefest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 简短（表语 too brief to do：母亲觉得它太简短，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 短暂（前置定语 a brief visit in spring：叔叔把整件事称作一桩短暂的短访）
F. adj. 短暂（同级比较 as brief as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩春天的短访相比）
G. adj. 短暂（后置定语 something brief：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 短暂（受程度副词修饰 quite brief：那位船工的评价）

items.q: a brief note on the table
the briefest note on the table anybody
The briefest visit in spring in

answers.why: brief 意为“简短”，1948 年渔人在航海日志里记下的是“一件简短的字条”，此处作前置定语 a brief note on the table。
brief 意为“简短”，此处用比较级 briefer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
brief 意为“简短”，航海日志上 七月 那行字说它是渔港里最简短的一件，故用最高级 the briefest note on the table。
brief 意为“简短”，母亲认为这件东西“太简短了，谁也用不上”，too brief to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
brief 意为“短暂”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩短暂的短访”，此处作前置定语 a brief visit in spring。
brief 意为“短暂”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩春天的短访一样短暂”，同级比较用 as brief as。
brief 意为“短暂”，航海日志上那半行字要的是“短暂的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something brief。
brief 意为“短暂”，邻渔港来的那位船工认为这套计划“相当短暂”，quite 修饰原级 brief。
brief 意为“短暂”，1958 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要短暂”，故用比较级 briefer than。
brief 意为“短暂”，母亲 1960 年说的是“整个渔港里最短暂的那一桩”，故用最高级 the briefest visit in spring。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1948 年，渔人在航海日志里记下了一件简短的字条。（a brief note on the table）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更简短。（briefer than …）
母亲觉得它太简短，谁也用不上。（too brief to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩短暂的短访。（a brief visit in spring）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩春天的短访一样短暂。（as brief as …）
到了 1955 年，航海日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件短暂的东西。（something brief）
answers: In 1948 the fisherman wrote of a brief note on the table in the logbook.
Everybody said it was briefer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too brief to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a brief visit in spring.
He said nobody would call it as brief as the visit in spring they had once had.
By 1955 the logbook asked for nothing but something brief.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 brief 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1948 the fisherman wrote of a brief note on the table in the logbook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the briefest note on the table in the harbour, or so the logbook says.
My mother thought it too brief to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a brief visit in spring, and nobody argued with him.
The boatman from the next harbour called the plan quite brief, and everybody laughed.
The brief ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
